findingsCorrected.priorGap: The reference detailed the shared root CAS and all writers but did not describe how the expected version must protect the state actually used by the invariant.
findingsCorrected.evidence: Jakarta Persistence 3.2 section 3.5.1 pairs version with data read. PostgreSQL 17 section 13.2.1 permits different committed snapshots for successive SELECT statements, supporting the explicitly described interleaving.
findingsCorrected.consequence: A loader can read total eight, let a competing writer commit ten/version two, then read version two and approve two more from the stale total; its CAS can still succeed.
findingsCorrected.correction: Added the concrete read-phase counterexample, consistent-state/version or qualified version-before-authoritative-read options, cache/replica and database/isolation checks, and prohibition on refreshing only the token while retaining old children.
findingsCorrected.guard: The alternative is explicitly conditional on every invariant-bearing writer atomically advancing the same root version. It is not a universal loading order or isolation prescription.
findingsCorrected.verificationChange: Expanded the deterministic target-database check to interleave a commit between invariant-state and version reads, while retaining the explicit limitation of in-memory/single-threaded evidence.

preserved: Concrete invariant/counterexample before boundary selection; no automatic inference from ORM graphs, table names, screens or child IDs.
Small aggregate as a conditional design choice, with legitimate alternatives for strict cross-root rules and no invented eventual-consistency allowance.
Typed domain identity, child-scoped identity, equality/proxy cautions and distinct persistence surrogate identity.
Root-mediated mutations and immutable child snapshots; List.copyOf protects only the collection unless elements are immutable.
Expected rejection preserves state/audit/events; candidate-state validation and deliberate fluent-versus-void contract.
Creation versus rehydration, stable historical facts, no new ID/time/events on load and no command replay.
Shared root concurrency protocol, same-transaction children, row-count failure and all ordinary/bulk/admin writers.

# Orders review fixture

This project targets Java 17 with JDBC and PostgreSQL 17. Production uses one primary database, no read replica or application cache. Each command obtains its own connection, uses READ COMMITTED and owns its transaction.

A committed order may contain at most ten units across all its lines. This is a strict business invariant, including simultaneous requests; delayed repair and overselling are not accepted. Starting with eight units, either request may add two, but both must not commit those additions.

The deployed entry point is AggregateFixture.add, using config/application.properties. HTTP, import and maintenance entry points all call it. In this fixture there are no additional child writers, deletions, mutable limits, triggers or externally published events. Distinct callers use distinct new line IDs. Existing state satisfies the invariant. Both reader implementations are shipped for compatibility, but only the configured reader is reached by this entry point.

Review this stated coverage; do not infer the same writer inventory for another application. The schema and source are supplied; no live database instance or PostgreSQL JDBC driver is included. Use an already available disposable target database if appropriate, otherwise provide a reproducible interleaving and identify the unexecuted integration check. Do not install a database or claim that source compilation proves isolation.

Compile the source, if a compatible local toolchain is available:
javac --release 17 -d classes src/AggregateFixture.java

db/schema.sql is a fresh-schema fixture for an isolated database only. No root/child redesign, framework migration or benchmark is requested. Preserve the strict business invariant and existing command outcomes.

prerequisites: A disposable workspace; any compilation uses an available JDK with --release 17. No dependency download is required for compilation because java.sql and javax.sql are JDK modules.
For an integration run, an already available isolated PostgreSQL 17 database and JDBC driver/runner or psql sessions are required. They are not provided or presumed available.
caseInputs.provenance: Synthetic development fixture authored for this review; not a real application or held-out example.
reproduction: Inspect config/application.properties and AggregateFixture.readPath/add/load to establish the active reader and common writer protocol.
Optionally compile src/AggregateFixture.java using the README command; this does not execute SQL.

If an isolated target database is available, apply db/schema.sql only there and reproduce the selected load and add sequences with two sessions and deterministic barriers; record the actual database version, isolation, statements, affected row counts and commit outcomes.

sources.title: Jakarta Persistence 3.2
sources.supports: Version is associated with the state read and checked when updating. Entity-owned state is not automatically an aggregate-wide guard; mixed versioned/unversioned objects do not gain whole-graph consistency. Bulk updates bypass automatic optimistic checks and do not synchronize the persistence context.
sources.application: Corrected the broken source link, supported the read/version pairing clarification and preserved the existing all-writers/JPA caveats.
sources.limits: Specification review, not a provider/JPA/target-database integration run. No framework migration is implied.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 17 Transaction Isolation
sources.supports: Separate ordinary SELECT statements in one transaction can see different committed snapshots. A single SELECT has a statement snapshot; concurrent updates re-evaluate the WHERE condition against the updated target row.
sources.application: Supports the admitted mixed-read counterexample and the bounded reasoning for a consistent combined-query read plus shared root CAS. The writer-participation and authoritative-read assumptions remain explicit.
sources.limits: No PostgreSQL process or SQL integration was executed. PostgreSQL documentation does not establish another engine's behavior.
